public_rationale: The May 25, 2025 archive displays 112 cases, including 19 May-dated decisions and 15 April-dated decisions [e1]. That snapshot does not establish the database total when the May 24 post appeared [e1]. Assuming 112 cases at publication, using the November 30, 2022 launch as a proxy for when ChatGPT became popular yields about 0.87 cases per week through May 24, 2025 [e1, e2]. These figures are consistent with the numerical claim, but decision-month counts do not establish when cases were added or publicly reported [e1]. The publication-time total and comparable reporting pace remain unverified [e1].
limitations: The launch date is an evaluator-selected proxy, not evidence of when ChatGPT became popular [e2].
The snapshot does not establish May’s representativeness or an increase in hallucinations per AI use [e1].
May’s representativeness remains a condition on the trend statement, not an independently established finding.

statement.document_title: AI literacy, hallucinations, and the law: A case study

from_speaker: a bit less than one publicly reported case a week
our_interpretation: The total refers to the database as it stood when the post was published on May 24, 2025.
For the weekly calculation, November 30, 2022 is an explicit evaluator proxy for the beginning of ChatGPT’s popularity, rather than a date supplied by Marcus.

The plain reading of the qualified trend statement is that the observed May pace, if representative, exceeds the earlier pace of publicly documented cases. It does not establish an increasing error rate per AI use.
The representativeness clause is preserved as a qualification on a historical comparison, not treated as a forecast or an assertion that May was demonstrably representative.
The target period covers the cumulative comparison from the chosen popularity proxy through publication. The exact database-total component concerns the endpoint specifically.
criteria.support_condition: A publication-time database record establishes 112 entries; the stated averaging period yields somewhat fewer than one entry per week; and comparable dated entries show a higher May pace that would imply worsening if representative.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A publication-time record establishes a different total, the weekly arithmetic is materially inconsistent with the stated comparison, or comparable dated entries show that May’s pace was not higher.
